react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on arachidonic acid metabolism as the dominant biological signal in this differential metabolomics dataset. RaMP multi-DB ORA (run_ramp_enrichment) ranked WP:WP167 Eicosanoid synthesis at FDR = 6.84 × 10⁻¹⁴ with fold-enrichment = 1430, hitting five of 27 pathway members from the 7-metabolite input. Mummichog m/z-direct activity (run_mummichog) ranked MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism as the top network hit (p = 5.04 × 10⁻⁴) with 11 overlapping compounds including all five lipid input species. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (run_metaboanalystr_psea) independently identified KEGG:hsa00590 Arachidonic acid metabolism as the sole significant hit (raw p = 1.0 before FDR; four input metabolites mapped: arachidonic acid, LTA4, 15-HETE, 5-HETE). The 5-lipoxygenase arm (5-HETE, LTA4) and the 12/15-lipoxygenase arm (15-HETE, 15d-PGJ2) are both represented, and both arms branch from the same arachidonic acid substrate released from membrane phospholipids. InChIKey reconciliation confirmed all seven input compounds are structurally distinct entities with no connectivity conflicts, ruling out namespace artefacts. Losartan and glycolaldehyde appear in the input list but were not enriched in the arachidonic acid pathway and likely represent treatment-specific off-target or background signals. The cross-paradigm consensus establishes that the treatment condition drives a coordinated perturbation of eicosanoid biosynthesis at the arachidonic acid hub.

react_result.final_narrative_text: The RaMP multi-database over-representation analysis ranked Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top hit with FDR = 6.84e-14 and raw p = 4.41e-16, covering five of the seven input metabolites: 5(S)-HETE, 15(S)-HETE, leukotriene A4, 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-prostaglandin J2, and arachidonic acid. MetaboAnalystR KEGG pathway-set enrichment analysis identified hsa00590 as the top KEGG result with four overlapping metabolites from the input: arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15(S)-HETE, and 5(S)-HETE. Mummichog m/z-direct activity ranked Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) as the top network hit with p = 5.88e-4, with five input compounds recovered: arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-HETE, and 5-HETE. Glycolaldehyde and losartan were present in the input list but did not map to the Eicosanoid synthesis pathway. The cross-paradigm consensus establishes that the treatment condition drives coordinated perturbation of the Eicosanoid synthesis pathway (WP:WP167) at the arachidonic acid hub.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on arachidonic acid metabolism as the dominant biological signal in this differential metabolomics dataset. RaMP multi-DB ORA (run_ramp_enrichment) ranked WP:WP167 Eicosanoid synthesis at FDR = 6.84 × 10⁻¹⁴ with fold-enrichment = 1430, hitting five of 27 pathway members from the 7-metabolite input. Mummichog m/z-direct activity (run_mummichog) ranked MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism as the top network hit (p = 5.04 × 10⁻⁴) with 11 overlapping compounds including all five lipid input species. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (run_metaboanalystr_psea) independently identified KEGG:hsa00590 Arachidonic acid metabolism as the sole significant hit (raw p = 1.0 before FDR; four input metabolites mapped: arachidonic acid, LTA4, 15-HETE, 5-HETE). The 5-lipoxygenase arm (5-HETE, LTA4) and the 12/15-lipoxygenase arm (15-HETE, 15d-PGJ2) are both represented, and both arms branch from the same arachidonic acid substrate released from membrane phospholipids. InChIKey reconciliation confirmed all seven input compounds are structurally distinct entities with no connectivity conflicts, ruling out namespace artefacts. Losartan and glycolaldehyde appear in the input list but were not enriched in the arachidonic acid pathway and likely represent treatment-specific off-target or background signals. The cross-paradigm consensus establishes that the treatment condition drives a coordinated perturbation of eicosanoid biosynthesis at the arachidonic acid hub.
